frames.reason:
ALIGNMENT. All four raws (BEFORE run1/run2, PINNED run1/run2) show the same state and camera. HUD: ORE 1,380, GAS 278, SUPPLY 23/30, CLOCK 00:42; STRIKE GROUP 10 SELECTED, Vanguard, Assault infantry, 100/100, -54 . 47, IDLE. Crystals, harvesters, buildings and the infantry cluster sit at identical pixels. No hostile unit, order marker or combat feedback appears in any frame. The four crop sheets show the same bars, rings and bodies at the same crop coordinates. I count eight bars in the cluster (the preflight text listed five). All eight are present with identical positions and lengths in all four raws. Within each arm the repeats are indistinguishable by eye, except one ring pixel discussed below.

PATCH SEMANTICS. I checked all eight supplied patches against the crops and rejected none. The light facet (884-886,353-355) is on the right-most body's pale upper block, and its reference (891-893,353-355) is adjacent floor. The dark side (877-879,356-359) is the dark chest flank beside the cyan slit. The bar patch (825-840,316-319) is the top bar, with floor reference 5 px above. The ring pixel (890,361) is at the right extreme of the right-most arc. The four minimap patches sit on the L outline, the teal blob, the marker and the left frame line, with navy-interior or panel references. They remain single examples, and some references contain grid or edge content.

1) LIGHTEST FACES / DARK OUTLINES: preserved. PINNED lifts the whole scene (floor dark taupe to light khaki, bodies blue-grey to pale blue-white). Every body keeps its pale upper block, teal pad, dark chest with bright cyan slit and dark lower-left contact shadow. Edges are crisp and nothing is doubled or soft. The pale bodies stay separated from the lighter floor by cool-versus-warm hue and by the dark chest and shadow rims, and the dark parts stand farther off the floor in absolute value (dark-side sample step -0.081 to -0.145 Y). I see no face or outline that has merged into the floor. I cannot exclude a few-percent local change at individual face-to-floor edges, but none is visible.

2) THIN BARS: present and crisp, not confirmed fainter. Extents are identical and edges clean. PINNED bars are paler mint than BEFORE's sage green and sit on the lifted floor, where they stay clearly separate. The weakest-looking spots are where a bar crosses the palest faces: the right end of the bar at x~827-838,y~330-333 and the left end of the bar at x~839-845,y~326-329, both over the top infantry head. Mint on pale blue is closer in lightness than green on blue-grey was in BEFORE. The bar is still discernible there by tint, and every bar's full length stays readable across floor. All bars are full in this pose, so partial-fill and track contrast is untested. I could not visually confirm any bar as fainter. This is the main residual risk (see limitations).

3) RING ARCS: preserved. All arcs are present, continuous, 1 px and the same geometry in all four raws. PINNED arcs are brighter and more saturated cyan on the lighter floor. The faint antialiased stretches at x~833-840,y~395-397 and x~859-862,y~387 are faint in both arms, not newly broken. The right-most arc (x~870-892,y~357-374) is continuous in both PINNED repeats. The supplied single-pixel sample (890,361) has lower luminance separation in PINNED run2 (0.115 vs BEFORE 0.135/0.139) and higher in PINNED run1 (0.148), with RGB distance higher in both. I do not waive it numerically and I do not infer a loss from it, because the whole arc reads as visible as in BEFORE. The pixel varies about 7% between PINNED repeats (0.450 vs 0.417) against about 1% between BEFORE repeats. That looks like edge-coverage variation, not a fading arc, but it is endpoint evidence only.

4) MINIMAP: preserved. The frame line, L outline, marker and blob are at the same coordinates and colours in all four, against an identical navy interior (sampled Y 0.0091 in every arm). The only change is outside the frame: teal translucent panel to near-black. That makes the 1 px frame stand off its outside neighbour more (sample Y 0.248 against a neighbour of 0.088 before and 0.0116 now). It also leaves the navy interior almost equal in value to the panel, so the cosmetic fill step is gone. The playable boundary is still carried by the clearly visible 1 px frame and the L outline, so this is a cosmetic fill change, not a lost gameplay cue.

HINT BACKING / PANELS. The new black box at x944-1264,y634-664 covers only empty floor here: no unit, ring, bar, minimap, PAUSE button or pool (pool y>=703, PAUSE y>=680 lie below it). No cue is hidden in this pose. In other poses it would dim any world content behind that rectangle, which I cannot assess. Separately, the existing panels (resources, strike group, tactical overview, buttons) look near-black rather than teal at 80% alpha, which conflicts with 'no palette change intended'. Here it only raises text, progress-bar and button-border contrast, so I treat it as cosmetic, but it should be confirmed as intended in whole-kit review.

VERDICT. No gameplay cue is lost, missing, doubled or blurred, and I could not visually confirm any as fainter, so this narrow pose passes as NEUTRAL. I do not rate it IMPROVEMENT because the infantry-cluster cues are equal, not stronger; only the minimap frame-versus-panel separation and the building rings are visibly stronger. I give no credit to pinning, and I did not defer to the preflight IMPROVEMENT label.

reason: Narrow safety adjudication of the AI-attack pose only, not whole-kit approval. I opened all eight required images and both text inputs, then re-read the rings, bars and infantry crop sheets. BEFORE and PINNED show the same camera, HUD state and object positions in both repeats. Each of the four watch items was checked independently by eye on native frames and exact nearest-neighbour crops. Infantry faces and dark outlines, all eight thin health bars, every ring arc and the minimap outline, frustum, marker and blob are present, same-geometry, crisp and not blurred. I could not visually confirm any cue as fainter, so there is no confirmed loss. The brighter floor compresses the lightness separation of the palest thin overlays slightly, so I rate NEUTRAL rather than IMPROVEMENT. The only changes that look like net gains are the minimap frame against its now-black panel and the larger building rings. The new hint backing and the near-black panel fills are cosmetic in this pose and hide no cue. Pinning is credited with nothing.
limitations:
Method: only Read was used. There was no zoom beyond the supplied crops, no pixel diff and no measurement. Coordinates are converted by eye from crop geometry, +/-1-2 px. The L* numbers below are my hand arithmetic on the supplied linear-Y medians, not a new measurement. I did not open the AUTO frames or the L9 boards, so I rely on the stated scale 1 / 1280x720 / samples 4 for both AUTO and PINNED.

Main residual risk, unconfirmed: the lifted floor compresses the relative lightness separation of the palest thin overlays. The supplied absolute linear separations rise, but hand arithmetic on the supplied medians points the other way for the sampled bar. Its CIE-L* step from the floor patch above falls from about 26 to about 21, and its Y ratio falls from about 2.4 to about 1.9. The ring-edge pixel loses luminance step in PINNED run2, although its chroma step rises. Faces and dark sides keep about the same L* step. So the direction of 'weaker' depends on the metric. I judged none of these visibly fainter in the crops, so I did not call them confirmed. If the hard rule is applied as any reduction in relative lightness contrast, the bars (especially where they cross the palest faces) and the repeat2 ring-edge pixel are what would trip it. A cropped relative-contrast check, or a dark underlay on thin bars, would settle it before whole-kit sign-off.

Not assessable: the frame is a single static end-state at clock 00:42 with all 10 infantry idle, no hostile units, no order or attack markers, no combat or damage feedback and no partial or low-health bar fill. Enemy-colour readability, order and attack cues, bar fill-versus-track states, and whatever the hint backing dims behind x944-1264,y634-664 in other poses are therefore unassessed. Stills cannot establish temporal stability (shimmer on thin rings and grid in motion), exposure adaptation or pumping, sustained 30 FPS, or that the 33 ms / 200 draw / 400k-triangle gates and all effects stay unchanged. Matching repeats give endpoint repeatability only.

Attribution: no visual or FPS benefit caused by pinning is established. AUTO and PINNED both reported scale 1 / 1280x720 / samples 4, so the BEFORE-to-PINNED differences come from the candidate's tone, HUD and underlay changes, not from the pin. Any retention rationale is an explicit authored thin-cue readability/stability policy, not an engine scaler fix.

Other caveats: the measurement patches are single examples, not segmentation of every unit, so they do not prove global readability. The panel palette change (teal to near-black) conflicts with 'no palette change intended' and should be confirmed as intentional in whole-kit review. This is one pose, so whole-kit approval is still required.
